$comment: Desk grade (store pages, Steam review API quotes, press, aggregators). NOT hands-on play; no claim of having played or listened.

package.basis: Desk only: Steam store page/appdetails, Steam review API (229 English reviews sampled, all-language 995/1062 positive), Steam news patch notes and the vaporlens review aggregate; not played.

fun.source: desk estimate: below Melvor Idle (65.4) — similar spreadsheet-idle loop with a stronger loot/party build layer but weaker presence (bars, no SFX) and a reported post-level-100 slowdown; well above a mediocre idle RPG (30.8). 94% positive, median positive reviewer ~150 h.

evidence.quote: This has a 1980s interface, but all the mechanics are incredibly solid.
style is, as per usual, nothing to write home about with these kinds of games

dims.note: Portraits, item icons and progress bars; functional, no visual identity.

evidence.quote: it's still about bars moving left to right or visa versa
watching lifebars and skill timers go down

dims.note: Combat is shown as bars and timers.

evidence.quote: Everything is documented. Everything has a tooltip.
UI is just awful, way too much clicking all the time, unintuitive.
The game is praised for its easy-to-use, clean, and fluid UI.

dims.note: Split opinion; in-game Glossary and filters praised, click volume and menu jank criticised.

evidence.quote: The music is very generic and gets boring fast and surprisingly the game is missing sound effects
The catchy 'heroic' music loop sets the stage

dims.note: From review consensus only; never listened.

evidence.quote: It starts off a little slow, the tutorial guides you through the basics
the first few hours of the game felt a tad monotonous and repetitive
Steam Demo allowing you to play the game up to level 50

dims.note: Auto-salvage/auto-restart early; clear but repetitive first hours.

evidence.quote: once you hit 100 and it's time to grind towards 150 the game slows down considerably
as soon as you beat the campaign, progression completely breaks down and grinds to a halt
The layered end game content made the amount I could play exponentially larger.

dims.note: Good to level 100 (~40-50 h), then a contested wall.

evidence.quote: Each skill has 8 different passives to choose from allowing for a wide variety of builds.
still basically no interesting options. classes feel super limited.
requires you to actually enchant & plan skills and character combos

dims.note: 4 classes x 3 ascendancies, parties of 3, enchants, raids; some call early choices irrelevant.

evidence.quote: $5.49 one price; no DLC listed
limited to 24h but you only get resources from gathering but no items or xp
While offline your characters won't be fighting

dims.note: Fair single price, no MTX; but offline is gathering-only (24 h), so combat needs the app running.

evidence.quote: missing sound effects, which would be an easy way to make the snappy and fast UI feel great
This is super micro intensive and not in a fun way.

dims.note: Loot flood is the only reward signal.

evidence.quote: 1.3.0.8 to 1.3.0.14 bug-fix patches April-May 2026
442 hours played. Saved game just vanished.
I don't think I've ever encountered any bugs

dims.note: Active solo dev; isolated save-loss reports (not counted as kill: anecdotal, not a pattern).

evidence.quote: 500+ Equipment Items ... 100+ Monsters and 50+ Bosses
Estimated playtime to finish all content is around 300 hours.
infinite loop of same content regurgitated forever with just higher hp/dmg

dims.note: Long, but scaling reskins past the campaign.

evidence.quote: a Semi-Idle RPG with a strong focus on Character/Skill Progression, Item Hunting, and Inventory Management
It's build-crafting like you find in games like Diablo, poe etc but no pesky grind

dims.note: Rubric anchor (~50): clear 'idle ARPG loot' pitch, one twist.

evidence.quote: Platforms: Windows only; languages: English
controller_support: none listed
Added additional keybind options for Pause Mission, Restart Mission

dims.note: One platform, one language; keybinds exist.

learn.practice: Ship an in-game glossary/codex that unlocks per monster, item and stat as discovered, so the build space never needs a wiki.
learn.evidence: https://steamcommunity.com/app/1960270/reviews (recommendation 225803195; via store.steampowered.com/appreviews/1960270?json=1) — 'the game has a built in wiki in the form of the Glossary'

learn.practice: Run several parties in parallel as a mid-game unlock, so the second team is a fresh beat rather than more grind.
learn.evidence: https://steamcommunity.com/app/1960270/reviews (recommendation 165333085; via store.steampowered.com/appreviews/1960270?json=1) — 'the game throws you AN ENTIRE SECOND TEAM TO GEAR'

learn.practice: Loot filters plus auto-salvage early, so a high item rate stays a reward and not a chore.
learn.evidence: https://steamcommunity.com/app/1960270/reviews (recommendation 174433057; via store.steampowered.com/appreviews/1960270?json=1) — 'not using the filters and auto-scrapping settings correctly'

learn.practice: Avoid Lootun's lapse: offline that grants only gathering forces players to leave the app open; Idlever's uncapped full-sim offline is the differentiator to advertise.
learn.evidence: https://steamcommunity.com/app/1960270/reviews (recommendation 152083749; via store.steampowered.com/appreviews/1960270?json=1) — 'forced to let the game running in the background'
